subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status use live gateway memory-runtime health as the source of truth, or is the current `not checked` plus opt-in local plugin status behavior sufficient?
rationale: Current main mitigates the original wording but does not satisfy the live-runtime health signal requested here, and the open fork PR plus https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 leave competing fix shapes.

options.title: Use live gateway status
options.body: Make the broader live-gateway contract the canonical fix and require proof with a real external memory plugin.

options.title: Accept current behavior
options.body: Declare `not checked` plus opt-in local plugin status sufficient and close the related attempted fixes as out of scope.

options.title: Define passive plugin status
options.body: Keep local status only behind a passive plugin status contract that cannot start heavy runtime work.

recommendation.title: Use live gateway status
recommendation.body: Make the broader live-gateway contract the canonical fix and require proof with a real external memory plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history points to Vincent Koc on the central status/gateway/memory-runtime files, and this is now a product boundary choice rather than a narrow code typo.
